subject: Turning customer needs into a practical design
hook: Sketch, measure, 3D, check. Then we cut.
ig:
Sketch, measure, 3D, check. Then we cut. The order matters, because changing your mind on a screen costs nothing.

How we work on every bespoke project:

Your list and a rough sketch: what's wrong, what you need, what you like.
A proper survey of the room, including the awkward bits.
Finish samples, looked at in your own light rather than a showroom's.
A 3D design so you can see proportions, door swings and shelf spacing.
Changes made on screen until it's right.
Only then does anything go to the workshop.

Most changes people make at the 3D stage are small: a shelf moved up, a drawer swapped for a door, hanging rail raised for long coats. Small changes, but they're the difference between furniture that fits the room and furniture that fits you.

Thinking about a project? DM us the word PLAN and we'll send the consultation link.
fb:
People often ask what actually happens between "we'd like some fitted furniture" and the first panel being cut. This short clip shows it.

We start with your list and a rough sketch, measure the room properly, look at finish samples in your own light, then build a 3D design so you can see exactly what you're getting. Changes happen on screen, where they're easy. Only once you're happy does it go to our workshop in Hanley.

If you've got a room in mind, our design consultations are free and come with no obligation.
